thread:
ana-support: FYI - Customer (DataFrameCo) reporting that their users are being asked to reauth every ~5-10 minutes after we rolled the new device-trust policy yesterday. They say the session shows as active in the app but the browser prompts for MFA. Full ticket: https://zendesk.internal/55432 :eyes:

ana-support: Repro steps from the customer (they gave these):
1) Login via SSO (Okta) + device trust flow on Chrome 118
2) Use app for ~3-7 minutes, then the UI shows 'reauth required' and a modal to re-run MFA
3) Clicking reauth completes, app returns to normal for a short window then repeats

ana-support: Their note: "happens across devices and incognito. We think it's related to the policy change earlier that tightened device token TTL."

ben-oncall: Thanks — can you paste any browser console / network traces they sent?

ana-support: Pasted below (redacted session ids):
```
Request: POST /auth/reauth 200
Response set-cookie: session=eyJhbGci...; Path=/; Domain=.dataframeco.com; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Expires=Wed, 18 May 2026 12:34:56 GMT

Later request: GET /api/v1/user/profile 401
Response body: {"error":"session_invalid","reason":"device_jwt_mismatch"}
```

ana-support: And this from their debug logs on backend side:
```
[2026-05-18T12:39:03Z] session-checker: session_id=redacted user_id=4321 device_jwt=hashA -> policy_ttl=300s
[2026-05-18T12:44:08Z] session-checker: session_id=redacted user_id=4321 device_jwt=hashB -> device_jwt mismatch, rejecting
```

cory-eng-infra: Hm — device_jwt changing between requests suggests either token is being reissued by IdP or the client is dropping one cookie and re-registering device. Could also be our policy-sync service re-authorizing devices and rotating device-jwt. Did we push a change to device-token rotation window yesterday?

policy-sync-bot: Deploy: device-policy-sync v1.14 -> rolled at 2026-05-18T10:05:12Z to region-eu. Changes: tightened device_jwt TTL from 24h -> 5m when flagged as "session-transient".

cory-eng-infra: That's likely. If device_jwt TTL dropped to 5m then in-flight sessions that expect longer validity could be invalidated when a reissue happens. But the customer's timeline (reauth every 5-10m) matches.

ana-support: Customer says it started right after the policy push. They also tried clearing cookies and it still happens (so probably server-side token rotation).

ben-oncall: Can you get an example full request/response where the reauth occurs? We need to see cookie headers, and the `Authorization` header for device-jwt if present. Also need user agent and whether requests go through our CDN (I suspect yes).

eva-customer: I can share one of our traces: we see two Set-Cookie events very close together. One sets `device_jwt=hashA` and then later `device_jwt=hashB` without explicit re-login. The session cookie remains the same value. Only device_jwt changes.

frank-security: Security note: If device_jwt rotates without invalidating session cookie, that should be fine so long as our verifier accepts the new jwt. But if verifier expects continuity (e.g., we tie session -> device_jwt hash) then rotation can cause the mismatch. Did we change the lookup logic?

cory-eng-infra: Checking git history... PR #4923 changed the session verification code to tie session record to device_jwt fingerprint to harden stolen session cases. That landed w/ policy-sync pairing only last week. Combined with the reduced TTL this looks like a logic bug: when we rotate device_jwt we were supposed to update the session record atomically. It appears rotation issued a new device_jwt but didn't update the session mapping in the primary DB in the v1.14 rollout path.

ana-support: Customer impact: all users on the latest client experience transient reauth prompts; enterprise admin worried this will block automated integrations. They want an ETA to fix or a rollback plan.

cory-eng-infra: I'll open an internal PR to patch the atomic update path. Short-term mitigation: we can increase device_jwt TTL back to previous value (24h) for affected regions and kick a config rollback. policy-sync-bot shows a quick toggle exists.

ben-oncall: Do it. Also add a feature flag gating the fingerprint-enforcement until we verify the mapping update works reliably.

policy-sync-bot: Rollback action queued by cory-eng-infra at 2026-05-18T13:02:11Z -> device_jwt TTL restored to 24h for region-eu.

cory-eng-infra: Patch branch created: fixes/atomic-session-update. Tests included to ensure session.record.device_jwt is updated in the same DB transaction when rotation happens. ETA to staging: 60m.

frank-security: Once patched, let's run a replay against the customer's trace and confirm no 401s. Also need a postmortem note because this tightened policy + new enforcement had combined unexpected interaction.

ana-support: I told the customer we'll do a rollback immediately and follow up with a patch + staged rollout. They're asking for timeline for fix and if there's a workaround (no good workaround except rollback).

ben-oncall: Good. Also confirm if any other regions rolled v1.14. policy-sync-bot reports region-us still on v1.13.

ana-support: I'll keep the ticket updated. Will capture affected tenant IDs and sample session ids for the eng patch verification.

cory-eng-infra: After rollback, we should monitor `session_invalid` errors and device_jwt rotation counts. I'll add a dashboard tile and an alert: threshold > 5% of auth calls failing -> pager.

frank-security: Add a quick check for inconsistent session->device_jwt mappings in the DB; if > 0 we'll reject rollout. We'll include it in the deployment gate.

eva-customer: Thanks everyone. Hoping rollback helps. Please ping me when you want the traces replayed or we can give a live session to debug.

ana-support: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket and mark as escalated to infra.

ben-oncall: Marking this thread: :rotating_light: incident-candidate :rotating_light:

policy-sync-bot: Note: rollout partially rolled back at 2026-05-18T13:04:07Z (region-eu). Monitoring metrics for `auth.session_invalid` increased from baseline 0.2% to 7.8% during rollout window.

cory-eng-infra: I'll post the PR link when ready. For now we treat this as a high-priority bugfix.

ana-support: Closing loop for now, will reopen if customer sees issues after rollback.
